beats: There's a tiny boat hiding under your dishwasher. Its only job is to float.
It's a flood alarm, and when it floats, your dishwasher goes into emergency mode.
Under the tub sits a plastic tray, sloped down toward one corner.
Any leak, from a hose, a door seal or a cracked pump, runs down into it.
In that low corner sits a little foam float, right under a tiny switch.
Foam is much lighter than water, so even a shallow puddle lifts it.
As it rises, it presses the switch, and the control board knows there's a leak.
First, the board shuts the inlet valve, so not one more drop comes in.
Then it runs the drain pump nonstop to empty the tub.
But that pump drains the tub, not the tray, so the little boat stays afloat.
On many models, the alarm won't clear until the tray dries out.
So a floating piece of foam is quietly guarding your kitchen floor.
